subject: Items contain category scoring spaces greater than 1

messages.author: fecbe3dc811bed89
messages.subject: Items contain category scoring spaces greater than 1
parts:
Hi Phil,

My data consists of binary and polytomous items. I run following syntax, but always get error message:


itemnumPCM = 16
itemnumNRM = 1
allData = read.table("allData.txt")
allData[allData[,13]==5, 13] = 1
allData[allData[,14]==5, 14] = 1
allData[allData[,16]==5, 16] = 1

apply(allData,2,table) # see all categories in items

Q <- array( 0 , dim = c( itemnumPCM+itemnumNRM , 2 ))
Q[1:itemnumPCM,1] = 1
Q[itemnumPCM+itemnumNRM,2] = 1

itemtype = c(rep("gpcm",itemnumPCM),rep("nominal",itemnumNRM))

COV = matrix(TRUE, 2, 2)
diag(COV) <- FALSE # diagnoal elements
COV[1,1] = TRUE # bca no slope parameter used
cmodel <- mirt.model(Q, COV=COV)

sv <- mirt(allData, cmodel, itemtype=itemtype, pars = 'values')
Error in FUN(newX[, i], ...) :
  Items contain category scoring spaces greater than 1.
                    Use apply(data, 2, table) to inspect and fix


Any suggestions? Thank you.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Items contain category scoring spaces greater than 1
parts:
Hi KK,

Some of the variables have spacings larger than 1. E.g., why you use apply(dat, 2, table) the result is forced to be a list, and you can see that the 13th variable has spacings 

$V13

   0    5 
2982 2018 

rather than spacings that go from 0 to 1, and column 15 has 

$V15

   0    1    2    3    5 
 304   67  680 2711 1238 

so clearly the 4th category was missing. You'll need to relabel these to make it work (e.g., for $V13, change all 5's to 1's; $V15 change all 5's to 4's). There is a technical reason for this relating to other functions, but unfortunately it is the only workaround. Cheers.

Phil
